candidates: Use `warnings.warn` (not Python's `logging` module) for all user-facing messages in ASE dynamics classes; `warnings.warn` is the project-wide convention and is easier to capture, filter, and assert on from tests and downstream packages.

Class docstrings must be placed immediately after the `class` line (or on `__init__`), not at the top of the module file; a module-level string is not treated as the class docstring by Sphinx `autoclass` and will be silently ignored in the generated docs.

When adding an `rng` parameter to an ASE dynamics class, accept either a `np.random.Generator` instance or any seed value understood by `np.random.default_rng`; when `rng=None`, generate a seed via `secrets.randbits(128)`, construct the generator with `np.random.default_rng(seed)`, and report the seed via `warnings.warn` so users can reproduce the trajectory later.
Call `super().__init__(...)` rather than the parent class by name (e.g. `MolecularDynamics.__init__(self, ...)`) in ASE dynamics subclasses.

Factor multi-phase initialization logic in `__init__` into focused private helper methods (e.g. `_set_externalstress(...)`, `_set_barostat_mass(...)`) so that each helper has no side-effects beyond what its name implies and `__init__` remains a concise orchestrator of those helpers.

Avoid using special floating-point sentinel values (e.g. storing `0.0` to mean 'disabled') to enable or disable features; use `None` or explicit boolean flags so the intent is unambiguous and fragile float-equality comparisons are avoided.

When a `disable_X=True` constructor flag works by setting a secondary attribute to a sentinel value that is checked later in other methods, add an inline comment at every such check (e.g. `if self.barostat_gamma == 0:  # i.e. disable_cell_langevin=True`) so the control flow is traceable without reading `__init__`.

When a dynamics class has not been tested with ASE `Atoms` constraints, emit a `warnings.warn` at the earliest point where non-empty `atoms.constraints` is detected, making it explicit to users that this combination is untested.

New MD integrator classes must be registered in `doc/ase/md.rst`: add an `.. autoclass::` directive in the primary ensemble section (NVT, NPT, etc.) and include brief `:class:`/`:ref:` cross-reference notes in the summary or recommendation text of any other ensemble section the class can operate in.
In `pytest.warns` calls, always supply a `match=` regex argument to assert that the specific expected warning message was emitted, not merely that some warning of the correct type was raised.

Docstring parameter descriptions for arguments that only take effect conditionally (e.g. a scaling factor that is applied only when the primary value is `None`) must state that condition explicitly rather than implying unconditional behaviour.

Keep class-level and parameter docstrings accurate as the implementation evolves; whenever a class's capabilities or parameter semantics change (e.g. a class gains variable-cell support, or a parameter's role is narrowed), update the docstring immediately to match the current behaviour.

When dispatching on array shapes or other tuple-valued discriminants, use Python 3.10 `match`/`case` blocks instead of chained `if`/`elif`; ASE requires Python ≥ 3.10, so this syntax is always available and produces cleaner, more readable dispatch logic.

New cross-cutting functionality that applies broadly across multiple dynamics classes (e.g. auto-generating and warning about an RNG seed) should be implemented in the `Dynamics` or `MolecularDynamics` base class rather than in an individual integrator, and contributed as a separate, focused MR rather than bundled into a feature MR.
